The powder of heat-resistant Al-Si-Fe-Mn-Ni alloy used in this study was gas-atomized, whose nominal composition was measured by Inductively Coupled Plasma-Atomic Emission Spectroscopy (Perkin Elmer Plasma-400, ICP-AES).

The deposited alloy was prepared by BLT-A300 equipment from Xi'an Bright Laser Technologies Co., Ltd., the composition of which was determined by ICP-AES (shown in Table 1). Argon was used as the shielding gas, and the preheating temperature of the substrate was 80 °C. Printing begins when the oxygen content in the cabin is below 200 ppm.

Comparing the mechanical properties of the alloys with different parameters, sample formed at 350 W/1300 mm/s has better mechanical properties. The horizontal yield strength (YS), ultimate tensile strength (UTS) and elongation (EL) of the alloy are 353 MPa, 589 MPa and 3.8%, while the vertical YS, UTS and EL are 332 MPa, 529 MPa and 2.0%, respectively. As is mentioned above, the forming quality of the alloy under this process is also preferable, so it was selected as the optimal process parameter, with which the subsequent heat treatments were explored.

attributes.morphology: chain pattern along columnar grain boundaries
attributes.location: molten pool boundary and inside molten pool

evidence.quote: AlFe0.23Ni0.77 was found in the solid solution alloy, and the diffraction peak intensity of the Si phase increased significantly, revealing that the high-temperature heat treatment induced diffusive precipitation of supersaturated elements in the sedimentary matrix, and the ternary complex precipitated phases of Al-Fe-Ni were gradually formed due to the extremely low solid solubility of Fe and Ni in Al matrix.

Meanwhile, AlFe0.23Ni0.77 phase began to form. Differ from Fe, Mn precipitating as small particles at the molten pool boundary, AlFe0.23Ni0.77 is distributed both at the intersection boundary and inside the molten pool with a scale of around 500 nm, and a chain pattern of inter-grain morphology along the columnar grain boundaries can be seen inside the molten pool (Figs. 7 (e, g)).

attributes.morphology: large holes and tiny unfused pores

evidence.quote: Judging from the figure, there are very large pore defects on the surface of the alloy with a scanning speed of 1150 mm/s. These large holes are mostly metallurgical defects left from the element burning caused by excessive input energy. With the increase of the scanning speed, the pores diminish dramatically. When the scanning speed reaches 1600 mm/s, more tiny unfused pores appear in the alloy.

mechanisms.name: low diffusion rate of Fe, Mn and Ni

evidence.section: 4.1 Precipitation behavior and high temperature stability
evidence.quote: According to Eq. (2), at 275 °C, the diffusion coefficients of Fe, Mn and Ni are 1.46 × 10-21 m2/s, 9.45 × 10-23 m2/s and 6.81 × 10-18 m2/s, respectively. Much lower than those of Si, Zn, Mg, which are 8.57 × 10-17 m2/s, 1.03 × 10-16 m2/s and 4.90 × 10-17 m2/s.

The eutectic Si undergoes significant fracture after the solid solution treatment. The continuous network broke up to form chain-like spherical particles. It is worth noting that at this time, the matrix no longer contains Si (point A in Fig. 7 (f)), which indicates that the traditional solid solution treatment did not solidify the Si element into the matrix, but rather led to a substantial precipitation

After solid solution treated at higher temperature, the Ostwald ripening inevitably occurs as the solute sites in the parent phase are vacated with the massive generation of complex precipitated phases, and the Al–Si eutectic breaks up and disintegrates to form numerous microscopic Si particles.

After solution treated at higher temperature, the formation of AlFe0.27Ni0.77 means that a large number of solute atoms were desolvated and Si was able to diffuse through the matrix, thus enabling Ostwald ripening to take place. ... the strength of the alloy is therefore significantly reduced.
